title: Mast-o musir
subtitle: Persian yoghurt with shallots
excerpt: Mast-o musir is a Persian yoghurt dip made with shallots soaked in water to mellow their sharpness, then mixed through thick yoghurt with a little dried mint. It is served cold as a side dish with rice, kebabs, or bread and takes five minutes to make.
sourceNotes: Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life: Ancient Persian and Modern Iranian Cooking and Ceremonies (1986). Mast-o musir documented as a classic Persian condiment served alongside rice dishes. Margaret Shaida, The Legendary Cuisine of Persia (1992). Notes on the use of musir (Persian wild shallot) and domestic shallot substitutes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate. The shallots mellow further over time.

content.text: Mast-o musir is a Persian yoghurt condiment: thick yoghurt mixed with finely sliced shallots that have been soaked in cold water to soften their sharpness, and finished with dried mint. It is almost always on the table at an Iranian meal, served alongside chelow and khoresh. The musir in the name refers to a specific Persian wild shallot; regular shallots, soaked first, work very well.
Put the finely sliced {{shallot}} in a bowl of cold water and leave for 30 minutes. This removes the harsh, sharp flavour. Drain and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Mix {{greek-yoghurt}}, drained shallots, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{mint-dried}} together. Taste and adjust salt. Transfer to a serving bowl.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving so the flavours meld. Drizzle {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} over the top if using. Serve cold.

items.symptom: The shallots are still too sharp and pungent
items.fix: Soak in cold water for at least 30 minutes, changing the water once. The sharpness fades noticeably after soaking.

items.symptom: The yoghurt is too loose and watery
items.cause: Yoghurt brand contains a lot of liquid
items.fix: Use strained Greek yoghurt rather than regular yoghurt. Drain it through a muslin for an hour if needed.

items.symptom: The mint flavour is barely present
items.fix: Buy a fresh supply. Dried mint loses its flavour quickly. Crush it between your fingers before adding to release the oils.

items.symptom: The dish tastes flat despite correct seasoning
items.cause: Not chilled long enough before serving
items.fix: The flavours need time to develop together. Make it at least an hour ahead and refrigerate.

content.text: Mast-o musir is one of the standard accompaniments at any Iranian meal alongside rice: along with mast-o khiar (yoghurt with cucumber) and torshi (pickles), it sits at the edge of every place setting. The musir used in Iran is a small, dried wild shallot with a more complex, slightly garlicky flavour than a domestic shallot; it is sold in Iranian food shops. Regular shallots soaked in cold water give a milder result but are a perfectly good substitute. The dish is also commonly made with spring onions, which are faster to prepare and even milder.
